rationale: I'm making one change, to preprocessing: re-reference each recording to the common average, and estimate the Welch PSD with the median across 2-s segments instead of the mean. Recordings arrive with no artifact rejection and with each clinic's own reference. The median keeps a few blink, movement or electrode-pop segments from distorting the band powers. The common average makes the topography independent of the reference, which should help both CV stability and transfer to the external Mumtaz dataset.

I'm splitting the five broad bands into seven: low alpha (8–10 Hz) vs high alpha (10–13 Hz), and low beta (13–20 Hz) vs high beta (20–30 Hz). The MDD literature points to these sub-bands (more upper-alpha and high-beta activity, linked to rumination and hyperarousal), and the broad bands average those effects away. Round 1 showed that changing the reference hurt badly, so the original reference and the rest of the pipeline stay exactly as in the current best.

I'm adding a second model and averaging its probability with the current one. It's a logistic regression on Riemannian tangent-space features. The input is each condition's spatial covariance matrix: 1–45 Hz band-passed and trace-normalized, so it doesn't depend on amplitude scale. The band-power logistic regression stays exactly as it is, on the original reference. Because the models' probabilities are averaged rather than their feature sets merged, the spatial information is added without diluting the band-power model, which matters at small n. Band powers only describe each channel's spectrum. The covariance matrices add inter-channel structure (connectivity and topography), which the literature links to MDD.

The covariance model should use a filter bank instead of one broadband covariance. Each condition gets trace-normalized spatial covariances for 1–45 Hz plus theta (4–8), alpha (8–13) and beta (13–30), and all tangent-space vectors go into one logistic regression. The 1–45 Hz covariance is dominated by alpha, which hides any MDD changes in theta or beta topography and connectivity. Separate per-band covariances (each scale-invariant) keep those patterns visible, and the band-power logistic regression and the 50/50 probability average stay unchanged.

Both logistic regressions use a fixed C=0.1, but the two feature sets are very different sizes: 190 band powers versus about 1,520 tangent-space features from 8 covariance matrices. One fixed value probably over-regularizes one model and under-regularizes the other. This change picks each model's C separately with a subject-grouped inner CV on the training fold only (`ctx["groups_train"]`), scored by AUROC; the features and the 50/50 average stay the same.

I'm adding a third logistic regression on debiased weighted phase-lag index (wPLI) connectivity: all channel pairs, in the delta, theta, alpha and beta bands, for each condition. Its probability is averaged with the two existing models. The trace-normalized covariances only capture zero-lag coupling, which is dominated by volume conduction and the shared reference. wPLI captures lagged phase synchrony, which is reported to change in MDD (especially in the alpha and theta networks), is insensitive to amplitude scale and reference, and so adds information the current models don't have.

I'm adding a fourth logistic regression and averaging its probability with the existing three. It uses orthogonalized amplitude-envelope correlation (Hipp 2012), computed for all channel pairs in the delta, theta, alpha and beta bands, for each condition. The current models capture zero-lag covariance and lagged phase coupling (wPLI), but not slow co-fluctuations of band-limited power. That amplitude coupling is a separate mechanism, reported to be altered in MDD resting-state alpha and beta networks. Orthogonalizing removes zero-lag leakage, and the correlation does not depend on amplitude scale, so the feature should be robust to reference and amplifier differences.

I'm adding a fifth logistic regression, averaged with the existing four. It describes spectral shape per channel and condition: the aperiodic 1/f exponent, the individual alpha peak frequency and the alpha peak height above the 1/f background. The exponent is a robust log-log fit over 2–40 Hz that leaves out the 6–14 Hz alpha range. The current relative band powers mix the aperiodic slope with oscillatory peaks. MDD has been linked to a changed excitation/inhibition balance (the 1/f exponent) and to shifts in alpha peak frequency and power, and all three features ignore amplitude scale, which should help on the external Mumtaz dataset.

I'm adding a sixth logistic regression, averaged with the existing five. Its inputs are signal-complexity features per channel and condition, computed on 1–45 Hz band-passed 4-s epochs and aggregated by the median across epochs: Higuchi and Katz fractal dimension, permutation entropy, Hjorth mobility and complexity, and spectral entropy. The literature reports higher EEG fractal dimension and entropy in MDD (Hosseinifard 2013, Bachmann 2018). These nonlinear features describe the temporal irregularity of the waveform, which the current power, spectral-shape and connectivity models don't capture. They are also independent of amplitude scale, and the epoch median damps artifacts, which should help on the external dataset.

I'm adding eyes-closed vs eyes-open reactivity to the band-power logistic regression: the per-channel log ratio of EC to EO absolute power in each band and in total 1–45 Hz power. MDD has been linked to altered arousal/vigilance regulation and weaker alpha blocking, and the current features can't capture this because relative power is normalized separately within each condition. A within-subject EC/EO ratio still ignores amplifier gain, and I'm adding it to an existing model rather than as a sixth one so it doesn't dilute the average (the round-9 complexity model lost 0.011 that way). I haven't run this yet. Expected weakness: the external set is EC-only, so every external subject gets a ratio of 0. That only adds a constant offset, so ranking there should stay roughly intact.

The five models are currently averaged with equal weight, so a weak model drags the ensemble down (the round-9 complexity model cost 0.011 this way). This change weights each logistic regression's probability by how far its inner-CV AUROC sits above chance, max(AUC − 0.5, 0.01). That AUROC already comes out of the training-fold-only `LogisticRegressionCV` that picks each model's C, so it adds no extra fitting. The weights adapt to how informative each feature family is for MDD on the training data, and the features stay exactly as they are. I haven't run this, so the effect on the Dev score is unknown.

I'm adding a delta (1–4 Hz) covariance matrix per condition to the Riemannian filter bank, so it becomes 1–45 Hz + delta, theta, alpha and beta. The broadband covariance is dominated by alpha, so delta topography and zero-lag coupling are currently missing from the spatial model. Frontal and limbic slow-wave changes are reported in MDD, and wPLI and AEC already showed delta coupling carries signal. Each matrix is trace-normalized, so this stays independent of amplitude scale, and it extends an existing model rather than adding a new one that would dilute the average. I haven't run this, so the effect on the Dev score is unknown.

The covariance model now estimates each spatial covariance only from clean 2-s epochs. An epoch is dropped when any channel's 1–45 Hz log-variance is a robust outlier within that recording (MAD-z > 3), and at least half of each recording is always kept. TDBRAIN arrives with no artifact rejection, so a few blinks, movement or electrode-pop segments can dominate a second-order statistic like covariance. Rejecting them should sharpen the Riemannian model, which is the largest one. The rule depends only on each recording's own data, so it doesn't depend on amplitude scale and should transfer to the external amplifier. I left the reference and the other four models unchanged; round 1 suggests re-referencing was what hurt there. I haven't run this, so the effect on the Dev score is unknown.

Restricting the covariance model to clean 2-s epochs gave the largest recent gain (+0.015). I'm applying the same per-recording clean-epoch mask to every other model: band power, reactivity, spectral shape, wPLI and AEC. Blinks, movement and electrode pops still contaminate their Welch spectra, phase-lag estimates and envelope correlations, and the rejection rule depends only on each recording's own data, so it should transfer to the external amplifier. Not run yet, so the effect on the Dev score is unknown.

The Riemannian covariance model is the largest and strongest component. I'm adding within-subject augmentation to it: each recording's clean epochs are also split into 3 contiguous chunks, and a trace-normalized filter-bank covariance is computed for each chunk. The classifier is trained on these chunk covariances plus the full-recording covariances, using subject-grouped inner CV, and still predicts from the full-recording covariance. The aim is to teach the logistic regression directions that stay stable across within-recording state changes (vigilance and drowsiness drift, non-stationarity) rather than noise, and to give the ~1,500-feature model about 4× more training samples at small n. The other four models and the equal-weight average are unchanged. I haven't run this, so the effect on the Dev score is unknown.

I'm adding long-range temporal correlation features to the existing spectral-shape logistic regression: the detrended-fluctuation-analysis (DFA) exponent of the theta, alpha and beta amplitude envelopes, per channel and condition, over fixed 1–12 s scales. Linkenkaer-Hansen et al. (2005) reported a breakdown of long-range temporal correlations in theta oscillations in MDD. None of the current models measures how band-limited amplitude evolves over seconds; they cover power, spectral shape and spatial or phase/envelope coupling between channels. The DFA exponent is independent of amplitude scale, so it should transfer to the external amplifier. I'm adding it to an existing model rather than as a sixth one so it doesn't dilute the equal-weight average (in round 9 a sixth model cost 0.011). I haven't run this, so the effect on the Dev score is unknown.

I'm adding eyes-closed→eyes-open spatial reactivity to the Riemannian model, for each filter-bank band: logm(C_EC^-1/2 · C_EO · C_EC^-1/2), the EO covariance mapped into the tangent space at the subject's own EC covariance. The current covariance features describe each condition separately against a group reference, and the reactivity features only cover per-channel power. The change in spatial covariance structure is computed within each subject, and an identical linear mixing of both conditions (amplifier gain, per-channel gain, reference) cancels out exactly, so it should be robust. It also targets the altered arousal/alpha-blocking regulation reported in MDD. It is computed from covariances already in the feature matrix and appended to the existing covariance logistic regression, so it adds no extra model to the average. Not run yet, so the Dev effect is unknown; on the EC-only external set these features are all zero, as the EC/EO power ratios already are.

I'm adding EEG microstate features to the existing spectral-shape/temporal-dynamics logistic regression, for each condition: coverage, mean duration, occurrence rate, explained variance and transition probabilities of 4 maps. The maps come from a polarity-invariant modified k-means on GFP peaks of average-referenced 2–20 Hz clean epochs from all items, with no labels used. They are matched to the canonical A/B/C/D topographies so the map order stays the same on any dataset. None of the current models measures the sub-second switching of global brain states, and MDD has been linked to altered microstate dynamics. These features don't depend on amplitude scale or reference, and they go into an existing model rather than a sixth one, so the equal-weight average isn't diluted. Not run yet, so the effect on the Dev score is unknown. On an external set the maps are re-fit on that set's own data, so the A–D mapping assumes its clusters come out with similar topographies.

I'm adding within-recording spectral dynamics to the existing spectral-shape/temporal-dynamics logistic regression, rather than as a sixth model. For each channel, condition and band (theta, alpha, beta), two features are computed over clean 2-s epochs: the standard deviation of log relative power and its linear trend over time. The motivation is the vigilance-regulation account of MDD (Hegerl, Olbrich): patients show "hyperstable" vigilance, with less alpha fluctuation and less drift toward drowsiness. None of the current models measures how power changes over a recording. Both features are scale-free, because gain cancels in log relative power.

Frontal and posterior alpha asymmetry is one of the most cited resting-state EEG markers of MDD (Henriques & Davidson 1991). This round adds explicit right-minus-left log absolute-power contrasts for the 8 homologous 10-20 channel pairs (all bands plus total power, per condition) to the existing band-power logistic regression. A linear model on the current per-channel features could in principle combine the two channels itself, but under the standardized L2 penalty that contrast is costly to learn at small n; giving it directly makes the asymmetry hypothesis cheap to use. The contrasts are within-subject, so amplifier gain cancels, and nothing is added to the five-model average. I have not run this, so the effect on the Dev score is unknown.
